harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Held curl at its current version (curl-7.29.0-59.el7.x86_64) on node1 by adding `exclude=curl` to /etc/yum.conf [main], the native RHEL7/yum mechanism to prevent a package from being touched by `yum update`. yum-plugin-versionlock could not be installed because node1 has no enabled repos (offline), so the built-in exclude directive was used instead. Verified the setting is syntactically valid (yum parses config without error) and that curl's installed version is unaffected. Completed the mandatory single-node restart: captured pre-restart boot_id/uptime baseline, restarted node1 via sudo reboot, polled until reachable, confirmed a new boot_id (proving an actual restart, not just elapsed time), and re-verified post-restart that curl's version and the yum.conf exclude=curl hold both persisted, with the node reporting systemctl is-system-running = running.
actions_performed: Inspected node1 OS/package manager (RHEL 7.9, yum) and current curl version (curl-7.29.0-59.el7.x86_64)
Checked for yum-plugin-versionlock; found it not installed and no enabled yum repos to install it from
Added exclude=curl to /etc/yum.conf [main] section (after backing up the original file) as the native yum hold mechanism
Verified yum parses the new config without error and curl version is unchanged
Captured pre-restart baseline: boot_id, uptime -s, systemctl is-system-running
Rebooted node1 via sudo -n /sbin/reboot (backgrounded so the ack returned before disconnect)
Polled node1 until exec access returned
Confirmed boot_id changed (33b0e84c... -> 27b0bcd3...) and uptime reset, proving an actual reboot occurred
Post-restart: verified curl version unchanged and exclude=curl still present in /etc/yum.conf, and systemctl is-system-running = running

evidence.requirement: Baseline: current curl version and no pre-existing hold mechanism
evidence.summary: rpm -q curl shows curl-7.29.0-59.el7.x86_64; yum-plugin-versionlock not installed; zero enabled repos (repolist: 0), confirming versionlock plugin install is not possible offline
Backed up /etc/yum.conf, inserted exclude=curl under [main], confirmed with grep that the line is present

evidence.requirement: Hold configuration is valid and curl unaffected
evidence.summary: yum check-update parses config without erroring on the exclude line (only reports no enabled repos); yum.conf content confirmed with exclude=curl present; rpm -q curl still reports the original version

evidence.requirement: Pre-restart healthy baseline and boot identity for node1
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id 33b0e84c-4dd1-406a-8f89-2e8ceca97bd6, uptime -s 2026-08-26 10:34:49, systemctl is-system-running=running, and exclude=curl + curl version confirmed healthy immediately before restart

evidence.requirement: Restart acknowledgement and disconnect during reboot
evidence.summary: Backgrounded sudo reboot command acknowledged; subsequent exec calls timed out connecting to node1, confirming the node went down for restart

evidence.requirement: Changed boot identity proving actual restart
evidence.summary: Post-restart boot_id is 27b0bcd3-461a-48fb-99d1-906c694d7785 (different from baseline 33b0e84c...) with fresh uptime 2026-09-29 10:36:04, proving a real reboot occurred

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of curl version hold and node health
evidence.summary: After restart: rpm -q curl still curl-7.29.0-59.el7.x86_64, exclude=curl still present in /etc/yum.conf, systemctl is-system-running=running
